title: ACB trap against a Junior Engineer — discharge before the Special Judge, Jaipur

input.text: Lawyer-to-lawyer. Client is a JE, PHED. ACB trap case, alleged demand 14.08.2026 for passing a contractor's bill. Charge-sheet before Special Judge (PC Act), Jaipur. Sanction is two lines. The bill itself was approved on 02.08.2026 — twelve days before the alleged demand. Recovery memo p. 31 is from a third person, not from the JE. Question: BNSS 250 or 262? Is the sanction vulnerable at discharge? I want a four-ground discharge, COURT_SAFE only, no PENDING names. Hearing in three weeks.

drafts.title: 250 vs 262 mapping note
drafts.body:
SYNTHETIC / DEMO — gate-shaped worked example; NOT filing-ready. [PENDING] holes are deliberate.

FILE MEMO — 250 vs 262 mapping (JE / ACB trap, Special Judge, Jaipur)
To: Supervising advocate
Re: discharge application — correct provision and heading

1. Discharge before framing of charge: BNSS 2023, s. 250 / s. 262 — map to the forum. Legacy equivalent: CrPC ss. 239, 227. Status SECONDARY: pick ONE after reading the Special Judge's procedure; do not plead both as if interchangeable.
2. Why it matters: 250 vs 262 is the maintainability of the application, not style. The heading must carry a single section.
3. Legacy trap: pleading CrPC 227 in 2026 without a savings-clause explanation is a beginner tell; if 227 appears at all it is as the legacy equivalent, not the live provision.
4. Charge sections: PC Act 1988, ss. 7, 13(1)(b) as charged (VERIFIED — read the charge-sheet's actual sections).
5. Sanction: PC Act 1988, s. 19 / s. 17A as applicable (SECONDARY) — which one depends on the date and the nature of the official act. Whether 17A applies on these facts: [UNCONFIRMED].
6. Four grounds for the matrix: (a) hearsay demand; (b) third-party recovery (p. 31); (c) chronology 02.08 vs 14.08; (d) two-line sanction.
7. Any case-law name stays out until COURT_SAFE. A separate inherent/supervisory filing is its own proceeding — [PENDING — separate provision to be confirmed]; not a paragraph here.

Recommendation: fix the heading to one BNSS section after the supervisor confirms the forum procedure.

terminalOutcome.label: Supervised four-ground discharge draft; export without PENDING names
terminalOutcome.rationale: The file has a real chronology fight, but discharge is still a high bar and the section heading must be right.
terminalOutcome.nextAction: Map 250 vs 262, keep the four grounds (hearsay demand / third-party recovery / chronology / sanction) in a table, supervisor to grade any case-law names.

teachingNotes: 250 vs 262 is not a style choice. It is the maintainability of the application.
A two-line sanction is a ground, not a magic wand. Discharge courts still ask whether the charge is groundless on the papers.
If the 02.08 bill is a different bill, the chronology point evaporates. Check the number.
commonMistakes: Pleading CrPC 227 in 2026 without a savings-clause explanation.
Writing 'demand not proved' as if this were a trial argument.
Citing a famous trap judgment from memory.
seniorVariants: Ground 1 facts (papers), Ground 2 law (provision), no names until COURT_SAFE.
Ask for the sanction file under the accused's right to copies before the discharge date.
Keep a fallback: if discharge fails, a s. 528 BNSS / inherent argument is a different filing, not a paragraph in this one.
